strengths: The core idea of achieving agent-environment disentanglement in a self-supervised manner using proprioception and forward visuomotor prediction is intuitive, biologically inspired, and avoids the heavy supervision (CAD models or segmentation masks) required by prior work such as SEAR.

The proposed method is cleanly integrated into model-free visual RL (DDPG / DrQ-v2 framework) as an auxiliary loss, achieving solid empirical improvements over DrQ-v2 and matching or outperforming SEAR on simulated Meta-world tasks.

The qualitative experiments on the BAIR robot dataset provide nice visual evidence that the model can learn to predict robot motion while remaining largely invariant to background/environment dynamics.
weaknesses: The RL evaluation uses only 3 random seeds per task. Given the high variance and known instability of off-policy visual RL algorithms, 3 seeds is below the standard (typically 5 to 10 seeds) required for statistically sound conclusions.

The BAIR video prediction experiments are purely qualitative (visual examples in Figure 5 and 6). Standard video prediction metrics (e.g., PSNR, SSIM, FVD, or tracking/segmentation mIoU against ground truth masks) are missing, making it difficult to assess how well the disentanglement and generation truly perform quantitatively compared to established baselines.

There are several unfinished sentences and drafting errors throughout the manuscript: Figure 5 caption ends abruptly with 'See', Figure 6 caption ends with 'See', Figure 8 caption ends with 'See', Appendix A.2 states 'Es is a convolutional neural network with 7.' and mentions 'sum of the sizes of hs and hs' instead of hs and hp.

The requirement of a 50k-step motor-babbling phase is a heuristic necessity that introduces overhead and limits the policy from immediate goal-directed learning. A more thorough ablation and discussion of how baselines perform with identical pre-training / babbling steps would be needed to isolate the gain of the auxiliary prediction loss from additional exploratory coverage.

Evaluation is limited to a single simulator benchmark (Meta-world) and a single base RL algorithm (DDPG). Demonstrating generalization across different robot embodiments, different action/observation spaces, or harder benchmarks (e.g., RLBench, ManiSkill) would substantially strengthen the submission.

strengths: Compelling conceptual motivation: Learning self-awareness and agent-environment disentanglement through visuomotor prediction (conditioned on proprioception) provides an elegant self-supervised alternative to CAD models or ground-truth segmentation masks (such as those required by SEAR).

Interesting emergent phenomenon: The qualitative results in Section 4.2 (Figure 8) show that when the agent picks up a tool (the hammer), the tool is effectively integrated into the predicted visual body-schema, matching cognitive hypotheses regarding tool use and body schema extension.
Comprehensive appendix detailing architectures, hyperparameters, compute resources, and reproducibility details.
weaknesses: Unfinished text and formatting issues: Several figure captions and sentences in the text appear abruptly cut off (e.g., caption of Figure 5: 'Figure 5: Predictions on the BAIR Dataset. See', caption of Figure 6: 'Figure 6: Generation of an unseen trajectory. See', caption of Figure 8: '...See', dangling footnote reference in Section 1 on page 3 '...tasks.2', and typos in Appendix A.1/A.2 such as 'Es is a convolutional neural network with 7.' and 'sum of the sizes of hs and hs').

Lack of quantitative evaluation for agent disentanglement and video prediction: Experiments on the BAIR dataset (Section 4.1) only provide qualitative examples. The paper would be significantly stronger if standard visual prediction / disentanglement metrics (e.g., PSNR, SSIM, FVD, or segmentation IoU evaluated against ground truth robot masks) were reported to verify how cleanly the agent is separated from moving objects.

Limited statistical evaluation in RL: Experiments across 10 Meta-World tasks are evaluated using only 3 random seeds. Pixel-based continuous control RL algorithms exhibit considerable variance across seeds; running at least 5 to 10 seeds and reporting aggregate metrics (such as Interquartile Mean with stratified bootstrap confidence intervals) is necessary to ensure statistical reliability.

Mixed performance across benchmarks: The gains over DrQ-v2 and SEAR are task-dependent and not universally superior (e.g., in Bin Picking, DrQ-v2 substantially outperforms Ego-Foresight; in Door Unlock and Assembly, performance is virtually identical to SEAR).

Overhead and role of the 50k motor-babbling phase: The method requires a 50k-step motor-babbling exploration phase at the start of every task to learn the visuomotor mapping. While baselines perform standard task exploration from scratch, it remains somewhat ambiguous whether the benefits stem from the architectural regularization or the extended initial exploration/replay coverage.

strengths: The core motivation—disentangling agent and environment through self-supervised visuomotor prediction rather than relying on privileged ground-truth segmentation masks or CAD models—is biologically grounded and conceptually appealing for robotics.
The paper evaluates both visual prediction capability on a real-world dataset (BAIR) and downstream policy learning across 10 manipulation tasks in the Meta-World benchmark.
Qualitative visualizations (such as tool incorporation in the Hammer task) provide an intuitive demonstration of how bodily self-prediction can dynamically adapt when manipulating objects.
weaknesses: Multiple unfinished sentences and editorial errors degrade the presentation quality throughout the manuscript (e.g., Figures 5, 6, and 8 captions abruptly terminate with 'See', Footnote 2 on page 3 is dangling, and Appendix A.2 contains fragmented text such as 'convolutional neural network with 7. Layers 3 and 6...').
Empirical evaluation relies on only 3 random seeds in continuous control RL benchmarks, which is insufficient given the well-documented high variance of image-based off-policy actor-critic methods.

The 50k-step motor-babbling stage introduces a significant exploration confound: it is unclear whether performance benefits arise from the learned representations or from extensive random exploratory coverage collected early on, and baselines do not seem to benefit from an equivalent exploration budget.

The technical novelty is limited; the approach largely combines Denton & Birodkar's content similarity loss with standard action/proprioception-conditioned video prediction (similar to existing video forecasting architectures) as an auxiliary loss for DDPG/DrQ-v2.

The claim that prediction provides 'regularization' is largely heuristic, with no formal theoretical backing or deeper analysis demonstrating why penalizing visually unpredictable actions improves sample efficiency rather than simply constraining policy exploration.

strengths: Compelling and biologically motivated problem formulation: learning agent-aware visual representations without requiring ground-truth segmentation masks, CAD models, or external robot-masking pipelines.

Clean and intuitive architectural design: splitting the visual representation into a large static scene vector and a low-dimensional agent bottleneck rolled out via forward action-dynamics effectively induces self-environment disentanglement.

Comprehensive empirical evaluation across diverse domains (Meta-World, Distracting DMC, Hurdle DMC, and the real-world BAIR dataset), demonstrating competitive performance against mask-supervised (SEAR) and model-based (Dreamer-v3) baselines.

Informative qualitative analyses and ablations: gradient-saliency visualizations clearly show emergent agent specialization, and tool-handling demonstrations illustrate the dynamic incorporation of tools into the agent schema.
weaknesses: Reliance on pixel-level reconstruction: as evidenced by the results on Distracting DMC, the pixel-space mean squared error reconstruction forces the model to attend to task-irrelevant background variations, causing performance degradation relative to the standard DrQ-v2 baseline.

Dependence on an explicit motor-babbling phase: introducing a 25k-step babbling phase is substantial for sample-efficient benchmarks. It remains unclear whether baseline methods were granted a comparable random exploration / warm-up phase to ensure a strictly fair comparison.

Minor presentation issues and drafting errors: for example, on page 3 the text incorrectly cites 'the RL algorithm (8)' where Equation 8 does not exist (presumably referring to Equation 4), alongside small typos such as 'douple' (page 5) and 'bellow' (page 11).

strengths: Compelling conceptual motivation grounded in sensorimotor prediction and contingency awareness, proposing a self-supervised formulation to eliminate the need for ground-truth masks or CAD models used in prior agent-aware methods (e.g., SEAR, Know-Thyself).

Simple and effective design: combining an information bottleneck on the predicted feature space with fast-forwarded scene context features naturally encourages the predictive model to isolate controllable agent dynamics and attached tools.

Good empirical gains on manipulation tasks in Meta-World, showing improved sample efficiency and asymptotic performance compared to DrQ-v2 and the supervised SEAR baseline, especially on tool-use tasks.

Informative ablation studies analyzing the impact of feature bottleneck dimensionality, auxiliary loss weight, prediction horizon, and motor babbling duration, alongside honest reporting of failure cases (e.g., Distracting DMC).
weaknesses: Reliance on pixel-level reconstruction makes the framework vulnerable when the environment contains independent motion or rich distractors (as evidenced by the subpar performance on Distracting DMC), where the assumption that the context representation can represent the static background breaks down.

Dependency on a fixed, relatively long motor-babbling phase (25k environment steps) to discover the visuomotor mapping. On physical hardware, executing 25,000 steps of random extreme actions is often impractical and potentially unsafe.

Missing comparisons with other self-supervised auxiliary representation learning baselines (e.g., SPR or CURL). Without evaluating a general auxiliary dynamics baseline that does not disentangle the agent, it is harder to definitively decouple the benefits of agent-specific bottlenecking from the regularizing benefits of multi-step forward prediction.
Real-world evaluation on the BAIR dataset is strictly qualitative, lacking quantitative trajectory prediction/disentanglement metrics or downstream real-robot policy learning.

strengths: Unsupervised Agent-Environment Disentanglement: Unlike prior approaches such as SEAR that rely on ground-truth simulator masks or external segmentation systems, Ego-Foresight achieves agent-environment disentanglement in a fully self-supervised manner by combining an action-conditioned recurrent forward model with a visual bottleneck and a bypassed scene representation.

Dynamic Body-Schema and Tool Incorporation: The qualitative and quantitative results show that when the robot interacts with and grasps objects (e.g., in the hammer task), the tool naturally becomes integrated into the agent representation ha because its dynamics become predictable from the robot's motor commands, a key advantage over rigid CAD/semantic mask priors.

Comprehensive Empirical Evaluation: The method is validated across 25 RL tasks spanning Meta-World, Hurdle DMC, and Distracting DMC, as well as qualitative generalization on the real-world BAIR dataset. It demonstrates competitive sample-efficiency and asymptotic performance compared to DrQ-v2, the supervised SEAR baseline, and model-based Dreamer-v3.

Thorough Ablation Studies: The paper includes meaningful ablations analyzing the auxiliary loss weight, prediction horizon, agent latent dimensionality, and duration of the motor-babbling phase, providing clear insights into the role of each architectural component.
weaknesses: Vulnerability of Pixel Reconstruction in Complex Backgrounds: Because the auxiliary objective relies on pixel-level MSE reconstruction, performance degrades when confronted with dynamic or complex backgrounds (e.g., in Distracting DMC), where task-irrelevant visual variations disrupt the feature representation.

Reliance on Pre-training Motor Babbling: The framework requires a fixed initial motor-babbling period (25,000 steps of random exploration) to learn the visuomotor mapping before policy improvement becomes effective. In safety-critical or hardware-constrained robotics settings, unconstrained random exploration can be impractical or unsafe.

Static Camera Assumption: The underlying assumption that the scene features hs remain static while only the agent features ha are modulated by actions holds primarily for static camera viewpoints. If the camera moves (e.g., on a mobile base or head-mounted camera), ego-motion induces action-dependent optical flow across the entire visual field, which would break the current disentanglement mechanism.

Aggregate Metric Reporting: The aggregated scores in Figure 1 rely on a custom threshold-based metric (averaging performance at 85%, 90%, and 95% threshold milestones). Presenting standard statistical aggregate metrics such as Interquartile Mean (IQM) and performance profiles with bootstrapped confidence intervals would provide a more rigorous benchmark comparison.
